reviewMethod: Original-resolution inspection of both three-still sequences plus complete sequential inspection of all 48 decoded frames in each bound contact clip

answers.reason: Across both complete sequences, the sphere and basketball advance continuously, rotate under inertia, transfer momentum at contact and finish on physical support; no object jumps or glides into a final pose.

Frame-by-frame inspection shows continuous sphere-to-shutter and basketball-to-bottle contact without a sustained gap or deep interpenetration; the tight D1 angle is visually crowded but the surrounding frames resolve the edge relationship.
The shutter begins rotating only at the measured sphere contact, and every bottle response follows the basketball arrival; neither sequence contains a pre-contact reaction.
The shutter accelerates, overshoots and settles around its hinge. In H1, three bottles respond at different rates and only two remain down, avoiding synchronized choreography.

The wide views expose approach, the contact views keep the collision axis and affected bodies visible, and the effect views expose the open aperture or asymmetric bottle result rather than concealing the solve.
Native blur is visible on the fast basketball, sphere and responding bottles while silhouettes, seams, gate edge and contact direction remain readable.
D1 illumination grows spatially as the solved shutter clears the aperture; the source remains static and the opening geometry controls the revealed pool of warm light.

All three H1 bottles visibly receive propagated contact. Two settle horizontally while the left bottle returns upright, which is an acceptable solver-owned asymmetry rather than a required posed collapse.
Basketball seams and grain, bottle shoulders/caps/labels, the ribbed hinged gate, rails, aperture and receiver remain recognizable at their action distances.
The D1 ball rests beyond the opened hinged gate and the H1 bodies settle on the floor with distinct rotations and contact shadows; both end states are visibly supported by their simulated paths.

visualQualityDiagnosis.mainGap: The action is solver-owned and unstaged, but simple bottle construction, pristine surfaces, limited environment detail and a crowded D1 contact angle still make both pieces read as polished prototypes rather than finished live-action-quality product cinematography.
visualQualityDiagnosis.requiredNextLesson: Keep the exact no-final-pose and Bullet-ownership rules while increasing scale-aware collision fidelity, filled-bottle mass distribution, surface microdetail, environment wear and contact-camera clearance through reusable asset and cinematography semantics.

limitations: PASS establishes one restricted reusable physics-action grammar across two distinct rigid-body mechanisms on this M2 Max, not general autonomous filmmaking.
The visual result proves unstaged physical causality but does not establish photorealism, glass/liquid dynamics, deformation, secondary debris, sound or advertising-grade asset quality.
The D1 contact shot is mechanically readable across the full sequence but one isolated contact still is crowded enough to suggest edge penetration without adjacent-frame context.
